docs.title: CodeGuard
docs.text:
Static analysis that finds security anti-patterns in source code — fast, offline, and built to sit at every gate of your workflow (editor, pre-commit, pre-push, PR/CI, merge, scheduled audit) from a single config file.

Version 2.2

CodeGuard scans Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript for security issues (including source-to-sink taint tracking for Python), performance problems, and code-quality risks. Many findings come with a safe autofix. The VS Code and Zed extensions show everything live with quick fixes. Rule IDs, the Finding / JSON schema, config keys, and exit codes are a stable contract from 2.0, and upgrading never changes a CI exit code: scan and ci run security rules unless you opt into more categories.

docs.title: What it produces
docs.text:
Each finding carries a stable rule ID, a severity, a CWE/OWASP mapping, a precise location, and a plain-English fix suggestion. Output is human-readable text, JSON, or SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning.

myproject/auth.py:12:5  [CG-SEC-001] HIGH  SQL query built with string formatting
    12 | cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {uid}")
         ^
  → Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute("SELECT ... WHERE id = %s", (uid,))

1 finding(s)  (1 high)

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Category Python JavaScript / TypeScript Security SQL injection, shell injection, eval/exec, unsafe deserialization, hardcoded secrets, weak hashes, disabled TLS verification, random for secrets, tempfile.mktemp, and taint-tracked SQL / shell / eval / path traversal / open redirect eval / new Function, child_process.exec, DOM XSS, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, hardcoded secrets, Math.random() for secrets, weak hashes, disabled TLS verification, open redirect, path traversal, prototype pollution Performance list-literal membership in loops, += string building, range(len()), redundant .keys(), regex compiled in loops await in loops, JSON deep clone, spread in reduce, new RegExp in loops, array-literal lookups in loops Quality mutable defaults, swallowed exceptions, complexity, nesting depth, parameter count loose equality, empty catch, complexity, var

See the rules overview or run codeguard list-rules.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
discovery  →  language adapter (parse)  →  rules (analyze)  →  findings
                                                                  │
                          suppressions · baseline · severity  ────┤
                                                                  ▼
                              formatter (human · json · sarif · …)

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• engine/registry.py — RuleRegistry, the catalogue of rules. Rules self-register at import time; duplicate IDs are a hard error. The module-level REGISTRY singleton is what the runner uses.
  • engine/rule.py — the Rule base class. A rule detects exactly one concern, is self-contained, and holds no state between files.
  • engine/finding.py — Finding, Location, Severity, Category. Finding is a frozen dataclass and the atomic unit of output.
  • engine/runner.py — AnalysisRunner walks the filesystem, parses each file, runs the active rules, applies suppressions, and returns findings.
  • analysis.py — project-level configuration, discovery, baseline, and policy orchestration shared by editor integrations and CLI behavior.
  • lsp/ — a dependency-free stdio language server that publishes CodeGuard findings as native editor diagnostics for saved and in-memory source.
  • cli/ — the codeguard command (click) and the output formatters.
  • rules/ — built-in rules, grouped by category. Each is one file plus a vulnerable/safe fixture pair under tests/fixtures/.

docs.title: v2.0 additions
docs.text:
• lang/ — a language adapter layer. LanguageSupport implementations wrap a parser (stdlib ast for Python; tree-sitter for JavaScript and TypeScript) and hand rules a uniform SourceNode. Rules declare the languages they target.
  • config/ — config discovery (first codeguard.toml / .codeguard.toml / pyproject.toml [tool.codeguard] found walking up to the repository root) and the validated schema.
  • engine/discovery.py — .gitignore-aware file discovery with parallel scanning.
  • engine/fingerprint.py — stable finding fingerprints for baseline and SARIF.
  • engine/suppressions.py — language-aware suppression parsing with reasons and expiry.

The Rule → Finding contract and the RuleRegistry pattern are unchanged in shape; the rule method is renamed check → analyze(ctx) and takes a context object instead of a bare ast tree.

docs.title: v2.2 additions
docs.text:
┌──────────── codeguard.toml (categories, rule options, ...) ───────────┐
files ──▶ discovery ──▶ parse ──▶ dataflow (Python, lazy) ──▶ rules ──▶ supersedes ──▶ policy ──▶ output
                                                                │                                  │
                                                         Finding.fix / .related          CLI · SARIF · LSP
  • engine/dataflow/: intraprocedural taint analysis for Python. catalog.py lists sources, sanitizers, and propagators. python.py walks each scope once and records the taint of every expression. The runner computes it once per file, and only when an active rule sets wants_dataflow. Rules query it through ctx.dataflow.taint_of(node).
  • Rule.supersedes: after all rules run, a finding from a rule that supersedes another removes that rule's finding on the same line. That is how a taint finding (with its path) replaces the matching pattern finding without the rules knowing about each other.
  • engine/fixes.py: safe autofixes. Rules attach Fix(edits=...). Edits are applied to UTF-8 bytes, atomically per fix, skipping overlaps. The CLI (--fix) and the language server (source.fixAll.codeguard) share it.
  • Rule options: Rule.default_options, overridden per project under [rules.<ID>], validated against the declared names and types, and available as ctx.option(name).
  • Categories: categories in the config (default security for scan / ci, all in editors) selects which rule packs run.
  • lsp/: actions.py (settings, diagnostics, code actions, hovers), positions.py (UTF-8 byte ↔ UTF-16 conversion), summary.py (codeguard/summary), and server.py (protocol, scheduling, caching). See Editors for the protocol.

docs.title: Autofix
docs.text: Some findings come with a safe fix: a rewrite that provably keeps the program's behaviour. CodeGuard applies safe fixes only. When a rewrite might change behaviour (for example == to === on values of unknown type), the finding keeps a suggestion and no fix.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
codeguard scan src/ --fix-dry-run      # print the fixes as a unified diff, change nothing
codeguard scan src/ --fix              # apply them, then report what is left
  • --fix edits files in place, rescans them, and computes the exit code from what remains. A fully fixed tree exits 0.
  • --fix-dry-run exits as a normal scan would, so it can gate CI ("fixable issues exist").
  • Both respect suppressions and the baseline: muted findings are never rewritten.
  • Line endings, encoding, and every byte outside the edited span are preserved.
  • When two fixes overlap, the first is applied and the other is reported as skipped. Run --fix again to pick it up.
  • --fix cannot be combined with stdin (-).

JSON output carries each fix under fix and counts them in summary.fixable. SARIF output includes them as fixes, which GitHub code scanning shows as suggestions.

docs.title: Editors
docs.text:
• Quick fix: put the cursor on a finding and open the code-action menu (VS Code Ctrl+. / Cmd+., Zed Ctrl+. / Cmd+.). The fix is the preferred action.

  • Fix all in a file: the source.fixAll.codeguard code action. Run it on save:

    // VS Code settings.json
"editor.codeActionsOnSave": { "source.fixAll.codeguard": "explicit" }

    // Zed settings.json
"languages": {
  "Python": { "code_actions_on_format": { "source.fixAll.codeguard": true } }
}

  • Fix all in the workspace: VS Code command CodeGuard: Fix All Safe Issues in Workspace.

docs.title: Rules with a safe fix
docs.text:
Rule Rewrite Applied when CG-SEC-009 random.choice / getrandbits / randbytes → secrets.choice / randbits / token_bytes, adding import secrets the value is security-sensitive; signatures are identical CG-PERF-001 x in [a, b, c] → x in {a, b, c} elements are hashable constants and x is evidently hashable CG-PERF-004 for k in d.keys() → for k in d the receiver is a name or attribute CG-QUAL-101 == / != → === / !== both sides have the same evident type (typeof x == "string", a.length != 0) 
codeguard list-rules --fixable

docs.title: Writing a rule with a fix
docs.text:
Attach a Fix to the finding and set autofix = True on the rule:

from codeguard.engine.finding import Fix
from codeguard.engine.fixes import edit_for_ast_node

fix = Fix("Remove .keys()", (edit_for_ast_node(call, receiver_text),))
findings.append(self._make_finding(node=call, filename=filename, fix=fix))

Edit positions are 1-indexed lines and UTF-8 byte columns, end-exclusive, exactly as ast and tree-sitter report them. Add a fixed.* fixture next to vulnerable.*: the test suite applies the fixes and compares the result byte for byte.

docs.title: Baseline
docs.text: A baseline freezes the findings that exist in your codebase today so CI only fails on new problems. It is a small JSON file of finding fingerprints — fingerprints are stable across reformatting and line moves, so a baselined finding stays matched as the code around it changes.

docs.title: Create one
docs.text:
codeguard baseline create              # writes .codeguard-baseline.json
codeguard baseline create src/ -o ci/codeguard-baseline.json

docs.title: Use it
docs.text:
codeguard scan . --baseline .codeguard-baseline.json

Or point at it from codeguard.toml so every run picks it up:

[codeguard]
baseline = ".codeguard-baseline.json"

Baselined findings are hidden from the default output and never affect the exit code. --show-suppressed reveals them (tagged (baselined)); JSON keeps a "baselined": true field and SARIF emits a suppressions entry so GitHub code scanning dismisses them.

docs.title: Maintain it
docs.text:
codeguard baseline update   # add findings that have appeared since (keeps first_seen)
codeguard baseline prune    # drop entries whose finding no longer occurs

A good workflow: create once, prune on a schedule, and let PRs drive the count down — never update to sweep new findings under the rug.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Release notes for the codeguard-cli package. The editor extensions keep their own: VS Code and Zed. Changes not yet released are listed as fragments in changelog.d/.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Added a local Language Server Protocol command and a Zed development extension with workspace scanning, live warning diagnostics, and a local Markdown security dashboard for Python, JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, and TSX.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
• Exit codes 3 (config error) and 4 (internal error) are now distinct from 2 (usage error); 0 and 1 are unchanged. The scan --severity flag is a deprecated alias of the new --fail-on (which controls the exit code); --fail-on defaults to info.
  • The PyPI project is now codeguard-cli (the bare codeguard name belongs to an unrelated project). The installed command and the import package are both still codeguard. Install with pipx install codeguard-cli / uv tool install codeguard-cli / pip install codeguard-cli.
  • The rule API changed: Rule.check(tree, source, filename) is now Rule.analyze(ctx), taking a RuleContext, and every rule declares a languages set. Python rules that subclass the new AstRule keep their check_ast(tree, source, filename) method unchanged. A new codeguard.lang package provides the language adapter layer for the tree-sitter backends.
  • --format json now emits an envelope object — { schema_version, tool, rules, results, summary } — with a per-finding fingerprint. The previous bare-array output is available as --format json-legacy for one minor version and prints a deprecation warning.
  • Location.col (and end_col) is now 1-indexed to match editors and SARIF. JSON location.col values shift by one; SARIF column values are unchanged in effect (the formatter no longer adds its own offset).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Added codeguard.toml / pyproject.toml [tool.codeguard] configuration: include/exclude, fail_on, output, jobs, gitignore, [rules] enable/disable, per-rule severity/confidence_min, [severity_remap], and path-scoped [[overrides]]. Config is discovered by walking up to the repository root; codeguard validate checks it and a starter file comes from codeguard init. (#7)
  • Suppression comments gained governance: a reason: is expected (bare ones raise CG-META-001), an until=YYYY-MM-DD reactivates the finding once past (CG-META-002), the file-level keyword is now ignore-file[...] (disable[...] is a deprecated alias), and codeguard suppressions list [--expired] [--unused] audits every suppression with an active/expired/unused status. // comments work for JavaScript and TypeScript. (#9)
  • Added a .pre-commit-hooks.yaml (hook ids codeguard, codeguard-full, codeguard-ci) and a composite GitHub Action at action/ — uses: mevichitra/codeguard/action@v2 — that runs codeguard ci and uploads SARIF to code scanning. (#13)
  • Added six JavaScript / TypeScript security rules (the CG-SEC-1xx block): dynamic code execution via eval / new Function / string timers (CG-SEC-101), child_process.exec shell injection (CG-SEC-102), DOM XSS sinks like innerHTML and document.write (CG-SEC-103), React dangerouslySetInnerHTML (CG-SEC-104), hardcoded secrets (CG-SEC-105), and Math.random() used for tokens or secrets (CG-SEC-106). (#14)
  • Added the tree-sitter language backends for JavaScript (.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs) and TypeScript (.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts). SourceNode now wraps tree-sitter nodes as well as Python ast nodes, with child_by_field for named children. Grammars load lazily, so a Python-only scan never imports tree-sitter.
  • Directory scans now honour the repository .gitignore, skip vendor/tooling directories (.venv, node_modules, __pycache__, dist, ...) and generated files (*.min.js, *.d.ts) by default, and never follow directory symlinks. AnalysisRunner.run_files(..., jobs=N) fans a scan across a process pool with output identical to a sequential run.
  • Every finding now carries a stable fingerprint (scheme codeguard/v1) derived from the rule, the file, the enclosing function/class, and the normalized statement — stable across reformatting and line moves. SARIF output emits it as partialFingerprints, and it is the identity key for the baseline and diff workflows.
  • New codeguard ci command: diff-aware scanning for pull requests. It scans only files changed since the base branch (auto-detected, or --diff REF), applies the baseline, defaults to GitHub Actions annotations, and can also write a SARIF report with --sarif PATH.
  • New baseline support: codeguard baseline create / update / prune writes a fingerprint file of today's findings, and scan --baseline PATH (or baseline = "..." in config) marks those findings so they no longer fail the run. Baselined findings are hidden by default, revealed with --show-suppressed.
  • New commands: codeguard list-rules, codeguard explain <RULE-ID>, codeguard validate, and codeguard init.
  • SARIF output gained partialFingerprints, security-severity, helpUri, and CWE taxonomy tags on each rule.
  • Three new --format options: github (GitHub Actions annotations), rdjson (reviewdog), and junit (JUnit XML).
  • codeguard scan --diff REF restricts a scan to files changed since REF (merge-base with HEAD), including uncommitted and untracked changes.
  • codeguard scan accepts multiple paths, reads stdin with -, and gains --config, --exclude/--include, --fail-on/--exit-zero, --no-gitignore, -j/--jobs, -q/--quiet, and --no-color.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• CG-SEC-005 now flags os.system, os.popen, subprocess.getoutput, and subprocess.getstatusoutput with a non-literal argument -- these always use a shell and have no shell= keyword, so they were previously missed entirely. (#3)
  • CG-SEC-004 and CG-SEC-005 now resolve import aliases, so from pickle import loads, import subprocess as sp, and from os import system as sh are detected. A shared resolver (codeguard.rules._pyimports) handles this. (#4)
  • CG-SEC-001 no longer reports a false positive for a multi-part concatenation of string literals such as "SELECT " + " * " + " FROM t"; the whole + tree is checked, not just the outermost operands. (#5)
  • Added the missing .license-header.txt so the insert-license pre-commit hook passes on a clean checkout.
  • Fixed all in-repo GitHub URLs, which pointed at a non-existent codeguard-ai/codeguard org, to mevichitra/codeguard (including the SARIF informationUri).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Added a documentation site (docs/, MkDocs + Material) covering install, usage, exit codes, suppressions, output formats, CI, architecture, and a v2 migration guide; published to GitHub Pages on release.
  • Corrected the CWE reference for CG-SEC-003 in the README (CWE-95, matching the rule).
  • Filled in the "Migrating to v2" guide with the changes that have landed (package rename, 1-indexed columns, JSON envelope, --fail-on, exit codes 3/4, gitignore-aware discovery, rule API).
  • Rewrote the "Adding a rule" guide for the new AstRule / analyze(ctx) API and the import-alias resolver.

docs.title: Internal
docs.text:
• Added TreeSitterRule, a base class for JS/TS rules that walk a SourceNode tree, and codeguard.rules._jsnodes with call / argument / literal helpers. run_benchmark.py now also picks up .js / .jsx / .ts / .tsx corpus samples.
  • Changelog is now assembled by towncrier from fragments in changelog.d/.
  • Moved the abandoned FastAPI backend and the two React frontends (which shared no code with the CLI) into archive/; they are no longer built, tested, or released.
  • Overhauled CI: concurrency cancellation, pip caching, a Windows/macOS/Python 3.13 test matrix, a build-and-install smoke test, pip-audit, a docs build, an old-org URL guard, and a changelog-fragment check. The release workflow now runs lint, types, and tests behind a tag/version consistency check before publishing.
  • Seeded benchmarks/corpus/ with true/false-positive cases for CG-SEC-001, CG-SEC-004, and CG-SEC-005 (precision and recall 1.0 on the seed set).
  • Switched the build backend from setuptools to hatchling; the version is single-sourced from src/codeguard/__init__.py.
  • Test fixtures moved to tests/fixtures/<language>/<category>/<rule_id>/ and conftest.load_fixture gained a leading language argument, so JavaScript and TypeScript rules can carry their own fixtures.
  • scan and ci share a single implementation (codeguard.cli._run); the Finding model gains a baselined flag.
Initial alpha: AST rule engine, CLI (scan), and five security rules (CG-SEC-001..005) with human / JSON / SARIF output and inline suppression comments.

docs.title: GitHub Action (recommended)
docs.text:
name: CodeGuard
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write
jobs:
  codeguard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0        # `ci` diffs against the base branch
      - uses: mevichitra/codeguard/action@v2
        with:
          fail-on: high

Findings appear as inline PR annotations and in Security → Code scanning. See action/README.md.

docs.title: codeguard ci
docs.text:
The action wraps this command; run it anywhere:

codeguard ci --diff origin/main --sarif codeguard.sarif

ci scans only files changed since the base branch (auto-detected, or --diff REF), applies the baseline, defaults to GitHub Actions annotations, and uses the same exit-code contract as scan.

docs.title: Any CI, plain SARIF
docs.text:
- run: pip install codeguard-cli
- run: codeguard scan src/ --format sarif -o codeguard.sarif || true
- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
    sarif_file: codeguard.sarif

docs.title: pre-commit
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/mevichitra/codeguard
    rev: v2.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: codeguard            # staged files, on every commit
      - id: codeguard-full       # whole tree, on push
        stages: [pre-push]

docs.title: GitLab / other
docs.text: --format rdjson feeds reviewdog for inline comments; --format junit feeds any JUnit-aware dashboard.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
CodeGuard reads codeguard.toml (or .codeguard.toml) from your project, falling back to a [tool.codeguard] table in pyproject.toml. Discovery walks up from the working directory and stops at the repository root.

Generate a starter file:

codeguard init

Check a file:

codeguard validate

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
[codeguard]                       # in pyproject.toml this is [tool.codeguard]
include   = ["src/**", "lib/**"]  # empty = every supported file
exclude   = ["**/*.min.js", "tests/fixtures/**"]
languages = ["python"]
categories = ["security", "performance", "quality"]  # default: ["security"]
gitignore = true                  # honour .gitignore (default true)
fail_on   = "high"                # min severity that makes the run exit 1
output    = "human"               # default --format
jobs      = 0                     # 0 = one worker per CPU

[codeguard.rules]
disable = ["CG-SEC-002"]
enable  = []                      # empty = all (minus `disable`)

[codeguard.rules.CG-SEC-001]
severity       = "medium"         # remap this rule's severity
confidence_min = 0.8              # drop findings below this confidence

[codeguard.rules.CG-QUAL-003]
max_complexity = 20               # a rule option (see `codeguard explain CG-QUAL-003`)

[codeguard.severity_remap]
CG-SEC-005 = "critical"

[[codeguard.overrides]]
path    = "migrations/**"         # gitignore-style glob, repo-relative
disable = ["CG-SEC-001"]          # or ["ALL"]

CLI flags win over the config file. --config PATH forces a specific file.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning include / exclude list of globs [] Gitignore-style path filters. languages list all Restrict to these languages. categories list ["security"] Rule categories scan / ci run: security, performance, quality. Editors show all three unless this is set. gitignore bool true Honour the repo .gitignore. fail_on severity or "never" "info" Exit-code threshold. output format "human" Default --format. jobs int 0 Worker processes (0 = auto). baseline path — Baseline file; its findings do not fail the run. See Baseline. [rules] disable / enable list of IDs [] Turn rules off / restrict to a set. [rules.<ID>] severity severity — Per-rule severity remap. [rules.<ID>] confidence_min float — Drop that rule's low-confidence findings. [rules.<ID>] <option> per rule rule default Rule options such as max_complexity; codeguard explain <ID> lists them, and unknown names are an error. [severity_remap] table {} RULE-ID = "severity". [[overrides]] array of tables [] path glob + disable / enable.

Monorepo nearest-wins

Per-directory config resolution (a nested codeguard.toml overriding the one above it, per scanned file) is not supported. One effective config applies to the whole run; [[overrides]] with path globs covers most monorepo needs.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
The full guide lives in CONTRIBUTING.md at the repository root. In short:

  • Setup: pip install -e ".[dev]" then pre-commit install.
  • Tests: pytest. Types: mypy src/. Lint: ruff check src/ tests/.
  • Sign your commits: git commit -s (Developer Certificate of Origin).
  • Add a news fragment: any user-visible change to src/codeguard/ needs a file in changelog.d/ (see changelog.d/README.md). Changes to an editor extension add an entry to that extension's CHANGELOG.md. See Releasing.
  • Adding a rule: one rule module, a vulnerable and a safe fixture (plus a fixed fixture for autofix rules), a line in tests/test_rules/test_rule_packs.py, a docs page (python scripts/scaffold_rule_docs.py writes a starter), and registration in the package __init__.py.
  • Editor extensions: npm ci && npm test in editors/vscode; cargo test and cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip2 in editors/zed.

docs.title: Editors
docs.text:
CodeGuard ships a language server (codeguard lsp) and two first-party extensions that build a native experience on it. Analysis is local in every case.

VS Code Zed Any LSP editor Live diagnostics, coloured by severity ✓ ✓ ✓ Hover with data-flow path ✓ ✓ ✓ Quick fixes, suppressions, Explain ✓ ✓ ✓ Fix all in file / on save ✓ ✓ (code_actions_on_format) ✓ (source.fixAll.codeguard) Whole-workspace scan at startup, with progress ✓ ✓ ✓ Findings sidebar, status-bar counts, Security Overview ✓ Project Diagnostics + Markdown dashboard — Fix all in workspace, SARIF export ✓ — via codeguard/fixAll

Editors show security, performance, and quality findings by default, because diagnostics there guide rather than gate. CI keeps the project's categories (security only unless configured). Each editor can switch categories off.

docs.title: VS Code
docs.text:
Install the extension from editors/vscode (see its README) and the CLI (pipx install codeguard-cli).

  • Findings view (shield icon in the activity bar). Findings are grouped by severity, category, or file, with a severity filter and a count badge. Inline buttons apply a fix or explain the rule; the context menu also suppresses a finding or copies its fingerprint.
  • Status bar. 🛡 ⓧ 2 ⚠ 5 ⓘ 9; hover for a breakdown and a Fix all link.
  • Security Overview (CodeGuard: Show Security Overview). Totals, severity bars, categories, top rules, top files, and a button that applies every safe fix.

  • Fix on save:

    "editor.codeActionsOnSave": { "source.fixAll.codeguard": "explicit" }

  • Settings: codeguard.categories, codeguard.severity.map, codeguard.rules.disable, codeguard.scanWorkspaceOnStartup, codeguard.path.

docs.title: Zed
docs.text:
Install the dev extension from editors/zed and the CLI.

  • Findings appear in the editor and in Project Diagnostics (Cmd+Shift+M / Ctrl+Shift+M), which lists the whole workspace.
  • The rule link in each diagnostic opens a local Markdown dashboard. Set codeDescription to "help" to open the rule documentation instead.

  • Settings go under lsp.codeguard in settings.json:

    "lsp": {
  "codeguard": {
    "initialization_options": {
      "severityMap": { "medium": "error" },
      "categories": { "quality": false }
    }
  }
},
"languages": {
  "Python": { "code_actions_on_format": { "source.fixAll.codeguard": true } }
}

docs.title: Other editors
docs.text:
Any LSP client can run codeguard lsp over stdio.

Neovim 0.11+

vim.lsp.config("codeguard", {
  cmd = { "codeguard", "lsp" },
  filetypes = { "python", "javascript", "javascriptreact", "typescript", "typescriptreact" },
  root_markers = { "codeguard.toml", "pyproject.toml", "package.json", ".git" },
  init_options = { client = "neovim", categories = { quality = false } },
})
vim.lsp.enable("codeguard")

Helix (languages.toml)

[language-server.codeguard]
command = "codeguard"
args = ["lsp"]
config = { client = "helix", severityMap = { info = "off" } }

[[language]]
name = "python"
language-servers = ["pyright", "codeguard"]   # keep your existing servers

docs.title: Server settings
docs.text:
Send these as initializationOptions, or later as workspace/didChangeConfiguration with {"settings": {"codeguard": {...}}}. Every key is optional.

Key Type Default Meaning severityMap object critical/high error, medium warning, low information, info hint Per-severity editor level. off hides that level. categories object or list project categories, else all { "quality": false } or ["security", "performance"]. rules.disable list [] Rule IDs hidden in the editor only. scanWorkspaceOnStartup bool true Scan every file at startup, not only open ones. codeDescription help | dashboard help Where a diagnostic's rule link points. client string — Informational (vscode, zed, ...).

docs.title: Protocol reference
docs.text:
Standard capabilities: textDocument/publishDiagnostics (with relatedInformation for taint paths and the fix in data), textDocument/hover, textDocument/codeAction (kinds quickfix, source.fixAll.codeguard, source.codeguard.dashboard), textDocument/codeLens, workspace/executeCommand, and $/progress for workspace scans.

Commands: codeguard.lsp.openDashboard, codeguard.lsp.explain (rule ID), codeguard.lsp.scanWorkspace, codeguard.lsp.fixAll (optional URI; sends workspace/applyEdit).

Custom methods, for building editor UIs:

  • Request codeguard/summary → every active finding:

    {
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "generatedAt": "2026-10-09T10:00:00Z",
  "workspaceRoot": "/repo",
  "counts": {"total": 3, "bySeverity": {"critical": 1, "high": 0, "medium": 0, "low": 1, "info": 1},
             "byCategory": {"performance": 2, "security": 1}, "fixable": 2,
             "suppressed": 0, "baselined": 0, "files": 2},
  "files": [{"uri": "file:///repo/app.py", "path": "app.py", "counts": {...},
             "findings": [{"ruleId": "CG-SEC-011", "title": "...", "severity": "critical",
                           "category": "security", "line": 6, "col": 5, "endLine": 6, "endCol": 20,
                           "fingerprint": "...", "hasFix": false, "cwe": "CWE-78",
                           "helpUri": "...", "confidence": 0.85, "description": "..."}]}],
  "rules": [{"id": "CG-PERF-004", "title": "...", "severity": "info",
             "category": "performance", "count": 2, "hasFix": true}]
}

    line / col are 1-indexed, and col counts UTF-8 bytes (as in JSON output). Diagnostics use standard LSP positions (0-indexed UTF-16).

  • Notification codeguard/summaryChanged {counts}: sent (debounced) whenever findings change. Re-request the summary when it arrives.

  • Request codeguard/fixAll {uri?} → {edit: WorkspaceEdit, count} with every non-overlapping safe fix, for the client to apply.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
CodeGuard's exit code is a stable contract you can gate CI on.

Code Meaning 0 Completed; no findings at or above --fail-on (or --exit-zero was set). 1 Completed; one or more findings at or above --fail-on. 2 Usage error — bad flag, unknown rule ID, missing path. 3 Config error — invalid codeguard.toml. 4 Internal error — an unexpected exception.

--fail-on defaults to info, so by default any finding yields 1. Use --fail-on high to gate only on high/critical, or --exit-zero for a report-only run.

Suppressed and baselined findings never affect the exit code.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: The PyPI project is codeguard-cli. The installed command is codeguard.

docs.title: As a tool (recommended)
docs.text:
pipx install codeguard-cli
# or
uv tool install codeguard-cli

docs.title: Into an environment
docs.text:
pip install codeguard-cli

Requires Python 3.10 or newer. No database, no server, no network access at runtime.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/mevichitra/codeguard
cd codeguard
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pre-commit install

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src:ro" ghcr.io/mevichitra/codeguard:2 scan .

Tags: :2, :2.0, :2.0.0, :latest. The image runs as a non-root user with the working directory mounted at /src.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
codeguard --version
codeguard scan .

docs.title: Other channels
docs.text:
• GitHub Action: uses: mevichitra/codeguard/action@v2 — see CI integration.
  • pre-commit: the repo ships a .pre-commit-hooks.yaml (ids codeguard, codeguard-full, codeguard-ci).
  • Standalone single-file binaries and a Homebrew tap are planned for a follow-up release.

docs.title: Migrating to v2
docs.text: v2.0 is a large step up from the 0.1 alpha. This page collects every backward-incompatible change so an upgrade is predictable. It is filled in as each change lands on main; see changelog.d/ for the in-flight set.

docs.title: Package renamed: codeguard → codeguard-cli
docs.text: The bare codeguard name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project. Install codeguard-cli instead (pipx install codeguard-cli). The command (codeguard) and the import package (import codeguard) are unchanged. If you pinned codeguard in a requirements file, switch it to codeguard-cli.

docs.title: Location.col is 1-indexed
docs.text: Was 0-indexed. Adjust tooling that reads col from JSON output; SARIF column values are unchanged in effect (the formatter no longer adds its own +1).

docs.title: --format json is an envelope object
docs.text: { schema_version, tool, rules, results, summary }. Parse .results instead of the top-level array, or pass --format json-legacy (deprecated, one more minor version) for the old bare array.

docs.title: --fail-on replaces --severity for gating
docs.text: --fail-on {severity|never} controls the exit code (default info, so any finding still fails by default). --severity is a deprecated alias.

docs.title: Exit codes 3 and 4
docs.text: Config errors now exit 3, unexpected internal errors exit 4. 0/1/2 are unchanged — only broaden handling if you special-cased 2.

docs.title: scan respects .gitignore and skips vendor directories
docs.text: Directory scans skip .gitignored paths, .venv / node_modules / __pycache__ / dist / build / …, and generated files (*.min.js, *.d.ts). Pass --no-gitignore to restore the old breadth; an explicitly named file is always scanned.

docs.title: SARIF partialFingerprints
docs.text: GitHub code scanning re-keys existing alerts once on upgrade, then stays stable.

docs.title: Multi-language: JavaScript and TypeScript
docs.text: CodeGuard now scans .js / .jsx / .mjs / .cjs and .ts / .tsx / .mts / .cts (tree-sitter). Six rules ship in the CG-SEC-1xx block. pip install codeguard-cli pulls the tree-sitter grammar packages automatically; nothing to configure.

docs.title: Rule authoring API (custom rules only)
docs.text: Rule.check(tree, source, filename) → Rule.analyze(ctx); a languages attribute is required. Python rules subclass AstRule and keep check_ast(tree, source, filename); JavaScript / TypeScript rules subclass TreeSitterRule and implement check_tree(root, ctx) over a SourceNode.

docs.title: Suppressions require a reason; disable renamed
docs.text: Add reason: … to every # codeguard: ignore[…] — bare ones still suppress but raise the new low-severity CG-META-001. # codeguard: disable[…] is now a deprecated spelling of # codeguard: ignore-file[…] (still works). An until=YYYY-MM-DD that has passed reactivates the finding and raises CG-META-002. Audit with codeguard suppressions list.

docs.title: Test fixtures moved (contributors)
docs.text: tests/fixtures/<category>/<rule_id>/ → tests/fixtures/<language>/<category>/<rule_id>/, and conftest.load_fixture gained a leading language argument.

docs.title: Planned (not yet on main)
docs.text: Nothing outstanding — v2.0 is feature-complete pending release packaging.

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text: Select with --format (on scan and ci). Suppressed and baselined findings are omitted from every format unless --show-suppressed is given.

docs.title: human (default)
docs.text: Coloured terminal output: one header line per finding (file:line:col [RULE] SEVERITY title), the offending source line with a caret, the fix suggestion, and a severity summary.

docs.title: json
docs.text:
An envelope object:

{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "tool": { "name": "CodeGuard", "version": "…" },
  "rules":   [ { "id": "CG-SEC-001", "title": "…", "severity": "high", "cwe": "CWE-89", … } ],
  "results": [ { "rule_id": "…", "location": {…}, "fingerprint": "…", "baselined": false, … } ],
  "summary": { "findings": 3, "by_severity": {"high": 3}, "suppressed": 0 }
}

--format json-legacy emits the pre-2.0 bare array (deprecated, one minor version).

docs.title: sarif
docs.text:
SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning and other tooling. Includes a rules[] catalogue with helpUri, security-severity, and CWE taxonomy tags; every result carries partialFingerprints (stable across reformatting and line moves) and, when suppressed or baselined, a suppressions[] entry.

codeguard scan src/ --format sarif -o codeguard.sarif

docs.title: github
docs.text: GitHub Actions workflow-command annotations (::error file=…,line=…::message), one per finding — shows on the PR diff without a SARIF upload. This is the default for codeguard ci.

docs.title: rdjson
docs.text: Reviewdog Diagnostic JSON — pipe into reviewdog -f=rdjson -reporter=github-pr-review for inline PR comments on changed lines only.

docs.title: junit
docs.text: JUnit XML — one <testcase> per finding (<failure> for active, <skipped> for baselined). Feeds CI test-report dashboards.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
CodeGuard publishes three things, each with its own version and changelog:

Artifact Version lives in Changelog codeguard-cli (PyPI, Docker, GitHub release) src/codeguard/__init__.py CHANGELOG.md, built from changelog.d/ VS Code extension editors/vscode/package.json editors/vscode/CHANGELOG.md Zed extension editors/zed/extension.toml and Cargo.toml editors/zed/CHANGELOG.md

docs.title: During development
docs.text:
• Every PR with a user-visible change to src/codeguard/ adds a news fragment to changelog.d/ (see its README). CI fails without one.
  • A PR that changes an editor extension adds its entry under ## [x.y.z] - Unreleased in that extension's CHANGELOG.md. CI fails without one.

  • Preview the next CLI release notes at any time:

    towncrier build --draft --version X.Y.Z

docs.title: Cutting a CLI release
docs.text:
1. Pick the version with Semantic Versioning: any breaking fragment means a major bump, any feature fragment a minor bump, otherwise a patch.
  2. Set __version__ in src/codeguard/__init__.py.

  3. Build the changelog. This writes the new section into CHANGELOG.md and deletes the fragments it used:

    towncrier build --version X.Y.Z --yes

  4. Open a release PR with those changes. Its edit to CHANGELOG.md satisfies the fragment check.

  5. After it merges, tag the merge commit and push the tag:

    git tag -s vX.Y.Z -m "CodeGuard X.Y.Z"
git push origin vX.Y.Z

    The release workflow checks that the tag matches __version__ and that CHANGELOG.md has a ## [X.Y.Z] section. It then runs lint, types, and tests, publishes to PyPI and GHCR, and creates the GitHub release.

docs.title: Releasing an editor extension
docs.text:
1. Make sure the extension's CHANGELOG.md has a ## [x.y.z] - Unreleased section and that its version matches the manifest.
  2. Replace Unreleased with the release date, in the same PR that bumps the version or just before tagging.
  3. Build it from the Editors workflow artifacts or locally. vsce package includes CHANGELOG.md, and the Marketplace shows it on the extension page.
  4. After publishing, start the next ## [x.y.z] - Unreleased section when the next change lands.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: CodeGuard grows in phases. Each phase keeps the 2.0 stability contract: rule IDs, the Finding / JSON schema, config keys, and exit codes only ever gain additions.

docs.title: Phase 1 — 2.2 (this release)
docs.text:
• Security depth: intraprocedural taint tracking for Python with five source-to-sink rules (SQL, shell, eval, path traversal, open redirect), plus new pattern rules for weak hashes, disabled TLS verification, insecure randomness, and Express redirect / path-traversal sinks.
  • Performance and quality rule packs for Python and JavaScript / TypeScript.
  • Safe autofix: codeguard scan --fix, --fix-dry-run, and editor quick fixes.
  • Editors: severity-aware diagnostics, quick fixes, hovers, a fix-all code action, a VS Code Findings sidebar and Security Overview, and Zed settings passthrough.

docs.title: Phase 2 — 2.3
docs.text:
• JavaScript / TypeScript taint tracking. Sources req.*, location.*, process.argv; sinks from CG-SEC-101/102/103/109/110.
  • Same-file function summaries. Track which parameters of a function reach its return value, and recognise helper functions that sanitize.
  • Pattern rules confirmed by taint gain confidence and severity when a source is found.
  • Custom rules in a Semgrep-compatible YAML subset (pattern, pattern-either, pattern-not, metavariable-regex), loaded from the rule_paths config key.
  • New security rules: SSRF, CSRF exemptions, ReDoS-prone regexes, XXE, insecure cookies, JWT none algorithm or disabled verification, raw SQL through ORMs.
  • Distribution: VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX publishing; the Zed extension downloads a standalone server binary from GitHub Releases.
  • Overview trends: keep summary snapshots so the editor overview can chart findings over time.
  • codeguard serve --watch: a long-running daemon that shares the language server's incremental cache with other tools.
  • Zed context server (MCP) exposing the workspace summary to Zed's assistant. Zed removed extension slash commands, so this replaces a /codeguard command.

docs.title: Phase 3 — 3.0
docs.text:
• Go, Java, and Rust through tree-sitter.
  • Offline triage that fills Finding.triage (heuristics first: test files, sanitizer proximity; an optional local model later).
  • Standalone binaries and a Homebrew tap.
  • Cross-file analysis backed by a workspace symbol index.

docs.title: Suppressions
docs.text: Waive a finding with a comment. The leader is # for Python, // for JavaScript / TypeScript.

docs.title: Inline (one line)
docs.text:
query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {uid}"  # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-001] reason: uid is an int

const html = build(input); // codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-103] reason: input is sanitized above

Multiple rules: # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-001, CG-SEC-003] reason: ….

docs.title: File-level
docs.text:
Anywhere in the file:

# codeguard: ignore-file[CG-SEC-002] reason: this module generates test fixtures

(# codeguard: disable[…] is a deprecated spelling of ignore-file.)

docs.title: Reasons are required
docs.text: Every suppression should carry reason: <short explanation>. One without a reason still suppresses, but CodeGuard also raises CG-META-001 (severity low) at the comment — so unexplained waivers show up in review.

docs.title: Expiry
docs.text:
risky()  # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-005] reason: pending refactor  until=2026-12-31

After the date the suppression stops working — the finding is active again — and CodeGuard raises CG-META-002 (severity medium). The expiry is evaluated against today's date; pass --now YYYY-MM-DD to scan / ci / suppressions list to pin it for reproducible CI.

docs.title: Audit them
docs.text:
codeguard suppressions list              # every suppression, with status
codeguard suppressions list --expired    # only expired ones (exit 1 if any)
codeguard suppressions list --unused     # ones that no longer suppress anything
codeguard suppressions list --format json

Status is active (currently suppressing a finding), expired, or unused (the named rule doesn't fire there any more — safe to delete).

docs.title: Visibility
docs.text: Suppressed findings are hidden by default. --show-suppressed reveals them (tagged (suppressed)); JSON keeps "suppressed": true, and SARIF emits a suppressions[] entry with the reason as the justification.

docs.title: Taint tracking
docs.text:
Pattern rules see one expression at a time: os.system("ls " + name) is suspicious whatever name is. Taint tracking follows where the data came from. It reports a sink only when untrusted data actually reaches it, and shows the path.

app.py:11:5  [CG-SEC-011] CRITICAL  Untrusted input reaches a shell command
    11 |     os.system(cmd)
  ↳ line 9: Untrusted input: flask request.form
  ↳ line 9: Flows through: host = request.form["host"]
  ↳ line 10: Flows through: cmd = "ping -c 1 " + host

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Sink Replaces CG-SEC-010 SQL execute() CG-SEC-001 CG-SEC-011 shell commands CG-SEC-005 CG-SEC-012 eval / exec / compile CG-SEC-003 CG-SEC-013 file paths (request data only) — CG-SEC-014 redirects (request data only) —

When a taint rule and its pattern sibling fire on the same line, only the taint finding is kept. It has the higher severity and the explanation. If the taint rule is disabled, the pattern rule reports as before.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Kind Examples Confidence Request data (web) flask.request.args/form/json/values/headers/cookies/files/data/..., request.get_json(), Django/DRF request.GET/POST/body/data/query_params/META/COOKIES (also self.request), parameters of functions decorated with @app.route, @router.get/post/..., @api_view 0.85 Process input (local) sys.argv, os.environ, os.getenv(), input(), sys.stdin 0.6

Import aliases are resolved, so from flask import request as rq works.

docs.title: Propagation
docs.text:
Taint flows through:

  • assignments, augmented assignments, tuple unpacking, and the walrus operator;
  • f-strings, % formatting, .format(), +, and " ".join(...);
  • method calls on a tainted value (.strip(), .get(), .decode(), .lower(), ...), except ones that return a bool or position (.isdigit(), .startswith(), .find());
  • str(), os.path.join(), pathlib.Path(), urllib.parse.unquote(), json.loads(), base64.b64decode(), and similar;
  • containers: writing a tainted value into d[k] taints d;
  • loops (a value tainted at the end of one iteration reaches the next), and both arms of if / try / match.

docs.title: Sanitizers
docs.text: Wrapping a value in any of these makes it clean: int(), float(), bool(), len(), shlex.quote(), html.escape(), markupsafe.escape(), urllib.parse.quote(), re.escape(), os.path.basename(), werkzeug.utils.secure_filename(), bleach.clean().

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Intraprocedural. Calls to your own functions return clean values. A helper that returns request.args["x"] is not followed. Same-file function summaries are on the roadmap.
  • Validation checks are invisible. if name in ALLOWED: does not clean name. Suppress the finding with a reason once you have such a check.
  • Python only. JavaScript and TypeScript taint tracking is planned.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
codeguard scan [PATHS]...

PATHS are files or directories (default .). Directories are scanned recursively, honouring .gitignore and skipping vendor/build directories. Read from stdin with -.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Purpose scan Scan paths and report findings. ci Diff-aware scan for pull requests — see CI integration. baseline create / update / prune Manage a baseline file. list-rules List every registered rule (--format json, --language, --category, --severity). explain <RULE_ID> Full description, CWE/OWASP, and docs link for a rule. validate Validate codeguard.toml. init Write a starter codeguard.toml.

docs.title: scan / ci options
docs.text:
Flag Description --config PATH Use a specific config file. --format {human,json,json-legacy,sarif,github,rdjson,junit} Output format. See Output formats. --rule RULE_ID Only run the named rule(s). Repeatable. --category NAME Only run rules in this category (security, performance, quality). Repeatable. Default: the config's categories, else security. --fix scan only. Apply safe autofixes in place, then report what remains. See Autofix. --fix-dry-run scan only. Print the safe autofixes as a unified diff without changing files. --exclude GLOB / --include GLOB Path filters. Repeatable. --diff REF Only scan files changed since REF (merge-base with HEAD). --baseline PATH Findings in the baseline don't fail the run. --fail-on {critical,high,medium,low,info,never} Minimum severity that makes the run exit 1 (default info). --exit-zero Always exit 0 (report-only). --no-gitignore Do not read .gitignore. -j, --jobs N Parallel worker processes (0 = one per CPU). --show-suppressed Include suppressed / baselined findings in the output. -q, --quiet Only print findings. --no-color Disable colour (also honours NO_COLOR). -o, --output PATH Write output to a file. --severity LEVEL Deprecated alias of --fail-on.

ci additionally takes --sarif PATH (write a SARIF report as well) and, when --diff is omitted, auto-detects the base branch.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
codeguard scan src/
codeguard scan . --fail-on high --format sarif -o results.sarif
codeguard scan . --exclude "migrations/**" -j 0
codeguard scan . --diff origin/main --baseline .codeguard-baseline.json
codeguard ci --diff origin/main --sarif codeguard.sarif
codeguard explain CG-SEC-001

See Exit codes and Configuration.

docs.title: CodeGuard Product & Workflow Guide
docs.text: Fast, offline, zero-infrastructure static security analysis for modern engineering teams. Native support for Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript with single-configuration governance across your entire SDLC.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Product Vision
docs.text:
CodeGuard is a fast, developer-friendly static application security testing (SAST) tool engineered to eliminate security anti-patterns before code reaches production.

Following its v2.0 makeover, CodeGuard bridges the gap between lightweight linters and heavy enterprise SAST suites. It requires no server infrastructure, no database, no Docker daemon, and zero cloud API keys. Everything runs 100% offline, executing deterministic AST and Tree-sitter semantic analysis in milliseconds.

       ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │                             CodeGuard                                  │
       │   Fast • 100% Offline • Zero Noise • Unified Policy Across All Gates   │
       └───────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                                           │
         ┌───────────────────┬─────────────┴───────┬────────────────────┐
         ▼                   ▼                     ▼                    ▼
   [Local Editor]      [Pre-Commit]          [PR / CI Gate]      [Audit & Baseline]
   Sub-second scan     Block bad code        Diff-aware PR       Manage tech debt &
   while coding        before commit         checks & SARIF      track suppressions

docs.title: 2. Where CodeGuard Fits in Your Development Workflow
docs.text:
CodeGuard is designed around a multi-gated security model, ensuring that security validation happens continuously throughout the developer workflow rather than as a delayed gate at release time.

flowchart TD
    subgraph S1["1. Local Development"]
        A["Developer writes code\n(Python, JS, TS)"] --> B["Instant CLI scan / editor\ncodeguard scan src/"]
        B -->|Findings detected| C["Inline remediation with\nplain-English suggestions"]
        C --> A
    end

    subgraph S2["2. Git Hooks"]
        A -->|git commit| D["pre-commit hook\n(staged files only)"]
        D -->|Fail| E["Commit rejected locally"]
        D -->|Pass| F["git push / pre-push hook\n(full tree check)"]
    end

    subgraph S3["3. Pull Request & CI Gate"]
        F --> G["Open Pull Request"]
        G --> H["codeguard ci / GitHub Action\n(Diff-aware scan against base branch)"]
        H --> I{"Are there new findings\nabove fail-on threshold?"}
        I -->|Yes| J["Post inline PR annotations\nFail CI status check"]
        I -->|No / Baselined| K["CI check passes\nUpload SARIF to Security Tab"]
    end

    subgraph S4["4. Continuous Audit & Debt Management"]
        K --> L["Merge to main"]
        L --> M["Scheduled nightly/weekly audit"]
        M --> N["codeguard baseline prune\n(Track & ratchets down debt)"]
        M --> O["codeguard suppressions list --expired\n(Enforce temporary waiver expiry)"]
    end

docs.title: The 5 Gates of CodeGuard
docs.text: Gate Stage Trigger / Command User Experience & Outcome Gate 1: Inner Loop Local Dev & IDE codeguard scan <path> Developers get sub-second feedback in their terminal with exact line numbers, code carets, and direct remediation snippets. Gate 2: Pre-Commit Git Commit pre-commit hook (id: codeguard) Catches mistakes before they are committed to git history; scans only modified files in milliseconds. Gate 3: Pull Request CI Pipeline codeguard ci or GitHub Action Scans only changed files/lines against the PR base branch. Baselined legacy issues are ignored; only newly introduced vulnerabilities fail the build. Gate 4: Platform Security Code Scanning Dashboard --format sarif Feeds directly into GitHub Code Scanning, GitLab Security Dashboard, Reviewdog, or JUnit test reporters. Gate 5: Governance & Audit Scheduled CI / Maintenance codeguard baseline prunecodeguard suppressions list Ensures technical debt is reduced over time and temporary waivers (until=YYYY-MM-DD) cannot be silently forgotten.

docs.title: 1. Shift-Left Without Developer Friction
docs.text:
• The Problem: Traditional enterprise SAST tools take 15–45 minutes to run in CI, spit out hundreds of false positives, and deliver reports to security teams weeks after the code was written.
  • The CodeGuard Solution: CodeGuard runs in < 100 milliseconds locally or in CI. It gives developers immediate, deterministic feedback directly in their terminal and PR diffs, with concrete code fixes.

docs.title: 2. "Stop the Bleeding" Baseline Adoption (Zero Day-1 Friction)
docs.text:
• The Problem: Adding a new security tool to a legacy codebase often creates 500+ immediate alerts, causing teams to abandon the tool or disable rules.
  • The CodeGuard Solution: Run codeguard baseline create. CodeGuard fingerprints existing issues and stores them in .codeguard-baseline.json. From that moment on, CI will never break on existing legacy code—it only blocks new vulnerabilities introduced in active PRs. Teams can then prune debt incrementally.

docs.title: 3. Governed, Accountable Suppressions (No Rotting Waivers)
docs.text:
• The Problem: Developers routinely bypass linter/security warnings with # noqa or # ignore comments without justification, creating permanent blind spots.
  • The CodeGuard Solution:
  • Every suppression requires an explicit reason: # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-001] reason: sanitized by custom validator (Omitting a reason raises rule CG-META-001).
  • Suppressions can carry expiration dates: until=2026-12-31. (Once expired, the finding reactivates and raises CG-META-002).
  • Security leads can audit all waivers with codeguard suppressions list.

docs.title: 4. 100% Offline, Privacy-First Architecture
docs.text:
• No source code is ever sent over the internet or passed to an external LLM endpoint.
  • Ideal for air-gapped environments, strict compliance regimes (HIPAA, SOC2, FedRAMP, ISO 27001), and IP-sensitive proprietary codebases.

docs.title: 5. Predictable CI Contracts & Multi-Ecosystem Formats
docs.text:
• Built with strict semantic exit codes (0 clean, 1 findings, 2 usage error, 3 config error, 4 internal error).
  • First-class formatters for any pipeline: human, json (v1 schema envelope), sarif (OASIS 2.1.0), github (Actions workflow commands), rdjson (Reviewdog), and junit (CI test runners).

docs.title: 4.1 Multi-Language Engine
docs.text: CodeGuard features a unified analysis pipeline supporting: * Python: Standard AST analysis across .py and .pyi files. * JavaScript & TypeScript: High-performance Tree-sitter semantic tree analysis supporting .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, .tsx, .mts, and .cts. * Smart File Discovery: Automatically respects .gitignore, skips vendor/build artifacts (node_modules/, .venv/, dist/, __pycache__/), and ignores minified assets (*.min.js, *.d.ts). * Multi-Core Parallelism: Built-in worker process pool (--jobs / -j) for multi-core scanning across large repositories.

docs.title: 4.2 Security & Meta Rules
docs.text:
Every rule in CodeGuard has a permanent ID, standardized severity, CWE/OWASP classification, and actionable remediation guide:

┌─────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬───────────┬────────────┐
│ Rule ID     │ Description                                            │ Severity │ CWE / Ref │ Languages  │
├─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼───────────┼────────────┤
│ CG-SEC-001  │ SQL query constructed via f-strings, %, or .format()  │ HIGH     │ CWE-89    │ Python     │
│ CG-SEC-002  │ Hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens, or credentials  │ HIGH     │ CWE-798   │ Python     │
│ CG-SEC-003  │ eval() or exec() execution on dynamic/non-literal input│ HIGH     │ CWE-95    │ Python     │
│ CG-SEC-004  │ Unsafe deserialization (pickle.loads, yaml.load)       │ HIGH     │ CWE-502   │ Python     │
│ CG-SEC-005  │ subprocess() invoked with shell=True on dynamic args   │ HIGH     │ CWE-78    │ Python     │
│ CG-SEC-101  │ Dynamic evaluation: eval(), new Function, string timer │ HIGH     │ CWE-95    │ JS, TS     │
│ CG-SEC-102  │ child_process.exec() invoked with a dynamic command    │ HIGH     │ CWE-78    │ JS, TS     │
│ CG-SEC-103  │ DOM XSS sink assignment (innerHTML, document.write)   │ HIGH     │ CWE-79    │ JS, TS     │
│ CG-SEC-104  │ React dangerouslySetInnerHTML with dynamic values      │ HIGH     │ CWE-79    │ JS, TS     │
│ CG-SEC-105  │ Hardcoded credentials, private keys, high-entropy API  │ HIGH     │ CWE-798   │ JS, TS     │
│ CG-SEC-106  │ Insecure randomness: Math.random() used for security   │ MEDIUM   │ CWE-338   │ JS, TS     │

docs.title: 4.4 Centralized Configuration (codeguard.toml)
docs.text:
CodeGuard can be configured via codeguard.toml, .codeguard.toml, or [tool.codeguard] inside pyproject.toml:

[codeguard]
include   = ["src/**", "lib/**"]
exclude   = ["**/*.min.js", "tests/fixtures/**"]
languages = ["python", "javascript", "typescript"]
gitignore = true
fail_on   = "high"              # exit 1 on "high" or "critical" findings
output    = "human"             # default output format
jobs      = 0                   # 0 = auto-detect CPU cores
baseline  = ".codeguard-baseline.json"

[codeguard.rules]
disable = []                    # disable specific rule IDs
enable  = []                    # specify an allowlist of rule IDs

[codeguard.rules.CG-SEC-001]
severity = "critical"          # remap rule severity

[[codeguard.overrides]]
path    = "legacy_scripts/**"   # monorepo path-specific override
disable = ["CG-SEC-002"]

docs.title: 4.5 Packaging & Distribution Formats
docs.text:
• PyPI Package: pipx install codeguard-cli or pip install codeguard-cli (CLI command is codeguard).
  • Official GitHub Action: uses: mevichitra/codeguard/action@v2.
  • Pre-commit Hooks: Ready-to-use hooks in .pre-commit-hooks.yaml for commit-time and push-time gates.
  • Container Image: Lightweight Docker image (Dockerfile) for generic containerized runners (GitLab CI, CircleCI, Tekton, Jenkins).

Step 1: Initialize Configuration & Freeze Legacy Baseline

# 2. Generate configuration

# 3. Snapshot existing findings so CI doesn't block on day 1

Add .github/workflows/codeguard.yml: 

name: Security Scan (CodeGuard)
on:

permissions:

jobs:

docs.title: 6. Summary: Why Developers & Security Teams Love CodeGuard
docs.text:
1. For Developers: Instant local feedback, zero cloud lag, no broken builds on untouched legacy code, and clear, copy-pasteable remediation suggestions.
  2. For Engineering Managers: Rapid onboarding without slowing down delivery velocity or drowning sprint backlogs in false-alarm triage.
  3. For Security Teams: Continuous policy enforcement across Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript, transparent suppression audits with mandatory justifications, and native integration into centralized security dashboards via SARIF 2.1.0.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Every rule has a stable ID (CG-<CATEGORY>-<NNN>), a severity, and a fix suggestion. Security rules also map to CWE and OWASP. IDs are permanent: never renumbered or reused.

0xx IDs are Python; 1xx IDs are JavaScript / TypeScript.

Which rules run

codeguard scan and codeguard ci run security rules by default, so upgrading never changes a pipeline's exit code. Turn on more with --category performance or categories = ["security", "performance", "quality"] in codeguard.toml. Editors show all three categories by default. Rules named with --rule or [rules] enable always run.

docs.title: CG-META-001: Suppression comment has no reason
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: meta · Languages: all

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
A codeguard: ignore[...] comment that does not include reason: .... Unexplained suppressions rot: reviewers cannot tell why the finding was waived.

eval(expr)  # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-003]

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Add a short reason, and optionally an expiry date.

See Suppressions.

docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: meta · Languages: all

docs.title: What it catches

docs.title: How to fix

codeguard suppressions list --expired

docs.title: CG-PERF-001: Membership test against a list literal inside a loop
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: performance · Languages: Python · Autofix: safe (how it works)

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
x in [...] compares x against every element, on every iteration. A set literal {...} finds it with a single hash lookup.

Reported:

# Membership tests against list / tuple literals inside loops.
def count_sources(paths):
    n = 0
    for p in paths:
        if p.suffix.lower() in [".py", ".pyi", ".pyx"]:
            n += 1
        if str(p) not in (".", "..", "/"):
            n += 1
        if p in ["a", "b", "c"]:
            n += 1
    return n

Not reported:

# Outside loops, short literals, sets, and floats do not trigger.
if mode in ["r", "w", "a"]:
    pass
for x in items:
    if x in ("a", "b"):
        pass
    if x in {"a", "b", "c"}:
        pass
for x in items:
    pass
else:
    ok = x in ["a", "b", "c"]

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Use a set literal, or hoist a frozenset constant out of the loop.

codeguard scan --fix (or the editor quick fix) rewrites the example to:

# Membership tests against list / tuple literals inside loops.
def count_sources(paths):
    n = 0
    for p in paths:
        if p.suffix.lower() in {".py", ".pyi", ".pyx"}:
            n += 1
        if str(p) not in {".", "..", "/"}:
            n += 1
        if p in ["a", "b", "c"]:
            n += 1
    return n

The autofix is applied only when it is provably equivalent: rewrite the literal as a set when every element is a hashable constant (str / int / bytes / bool / None -- no floats, whose NaN and -0.0 compare differently) and the left operand is evidently hashable (a literal, an f-string, str() / int() / len() / ord() / repr(), or a string method such as .lower()). Anything else gets a suggestion only, because unhashable in {...} raises TypeError.

docs.text:
Set in codeguard.toml:

[codeguard.rules.CG-PERF-001]
min_elements = 3

docs.title: CG-PERF-002: String built with += inside a loop
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: performance · Languages: Python

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Repeated s += ... on a string inside a loop can copy the whole string each time, which is quadratic in its final length.

Reported:

def render(rows):
    html = ""
    for row in rows:
        html += f"<tr><td>{row}</td></tr>"
    return html


def csv_line(cells):
    out: str = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(cells):
        out += cells[i] + ","
        i += 1
    return out

Not reported:

def total(values):
    s = 0
    for v in values:
        s += v
    return s


def render(rows):
    parts = []
    for row in rows:
        parts.append(f"<tr><td>{row}</td></tr>")
    return "".join(parts)

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Collect the parts in a list and join once: parts.append(x); ... ''.join(parts).

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-PERF-002] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-PERF-003: for i in range(len(seq)) used to index seq
docs.text: Severity: INFO · Category: performance · Languages: Python

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
The loop iterates over indices only to look items up with seq[i]. Iterating the sequence directly (or with enumerate) avoids a lookup per item.

Reported:

def total(items):
    s = 0
    for i in range(len(items)):
        s += items[i]
    return s

Not reported:

def pairs(items):
    out = []
    for i in range(len(items)):
        out.append(i * 2)
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        out.append(item)
    return out

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Iterate directly: for item in seq, or for i, item in enumerate(seq).

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-PERF-003] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-PERF-004: Redundant .keys() in iteration or membership test
docs.text: Severity: INFO · Category: performance · Languages: Python · Autofix: safe (how it works)

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Iterating a mapping or testing membership already uses its keys; calling .keys() adds a method call and a view object for nothing.

Reported:

def show(config, settings):
    for key in config.keys():
        print(key)
    if "debug" in settings.options.keys():
        print("debug")
    return [k for k in config.keys() if k]

Not reported:

def show(config):
    names = list(config.keys())
    for key in config:
        print(key)
    for key in load().keys():
        print(key)
    return names

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Iterate or test the mapping itself: for k in d: and k in d.

codeguard scan --fix (or the editor quick fix) rewrites the example to:

def show(config, settings):
    for key in config:
        print(key)
    if "debug" in settings.options:
        print("debug")
    return [k for k in config if k]

The autofix is applied only when it is provably equivalent: drop .keys() when the receiver is a name or attribute.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-PERF-004] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-PERF-005: Regular expression compiled inside a loop
docs.text: Severity: INFO · Category: performance · Languages: Python

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
A regular expression with a constant pattern is compiled (or looked up in re's cache) on every iteration. Compile it once outside the loop.

Reported:

import re
from re import compile as rx


def emails(lines):
    out = []
    for line in lines:
        if re.match(r"[^@]+@[^@]+", line):
            out.append(line)
        pattern = rx("^#")
    return out

Not reported:

import re

EMAIL = re.compile(r"[^@]+@[^@]+")


def emails(lines, user_pattern):
    out = [line for line in lines if EMAIL.match(line)]
    for line in lines:
        if re.search(user_pattern, line):
            out.append(line)
    return out

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Compile once outside the loop: PATTERN = re.compile(r'...'), then PATTERN.search(s).

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-PERF-005] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-PERF-101: await inside a loop runs the iterations one after another
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: performance · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Each iteration waits for the previous await to finish. When the iterations are independent, starting them together with Promise.all is usually much faster.

Reported:

async function loadAll(ids) {
  const users = [];
  for (const id of ids) {
    users.push(await fetchUser(id));
  }
  let i = 0;
  while (i < ids.length) {
    await save(ids[i++]);
  }
  return users;
}

Not reported:

async function loadAll(ids, stream) {
  const users = await Promise.all(ids.map(async (id) => await fetchUser(id)));
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    await write(chunk);
  }
  return users;
}

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: If iterations are independent: await Promise.all(items.map(async (item) => ...)). Keep the loop when order or rate limits matter.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: // codeguard: ignore[CG-PERF-101] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-PERF-102: Deep clone with JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))
docs.text: Severity: INFO · Category: performance · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Serialising to a JSON string and parsing it back is slow for large objects and silently drops undefined, functions, Dates (become strings), Maps, and Sets.

Reported:

const copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(state));

Not reported:

const copy = structuredClone(state);
const parsed = JSON.parse(text);

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Use structuredClone(x) (Node 17+, all modern browsers). It keeps Dates, Maps, and Sets, but throws on functions.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: // codeguard: ignore[CG-PERF-102] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-PERF-103: Accumulator copied with spread inside reduce
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: performance · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Returning [...acc, x] or {...acc, k: v} from a reduce callback copies the whole accumulator on every step, which is quadratic in the number of items.

Reported:

const ids = users.reduce((acc, u) => [...acc, u.id], []);
const byId = users.reduce((acc, u) => ({ ...acc, [u.id]: u }), {});

Not reported:

const ids = users.reduce((acc, u) => {
  acc.push(u.id);
  return acc;
}, []);
const merged = items.reduce((acc, x) => [...x.tags], []);

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Mutate the accumulator (acc.push(x); return acc) or use a plain loop / Object.fromEntries.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: // codeguard: ignore[CG-PERF-103] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-PERF-104: new RegExp() with a constant pattern inside a loop
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: performance · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
A regular expression with a constant pattern is compiled on every iteration. Create it once outside the loop, or use a regex literal.

Reported:

for (const line of lines) {
  if (new RegExp("^\\s*#").test(line)) continue;
}

Not reported:

const COMMENT = /^\s*#/;
for (const line of lines) {
  if (COMMENT.test(line)) continue;
  if (new RegExp(userPattern).test(line)) count++;
}

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Hoist it: const PATTERN = /.../; before the loop.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: // codeguard: ignore[CG-PERF-104] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-PERF-105: includes() / indexOf() on an array literal inside a loop
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: performance · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Searching an array literal compares against every element on every iteration. A Set created once outside the loop answers with a single hash lookup.

Reported:

for (const file of files) {
  if (["js", "jsx", "ts", "tsx"].includes(file.ext)) total++;
}

Not reported:

const SOURCE = new Set(["js", "jsx", "ts", "tsx"]);
for (const file of files) {
  if (SOURCE.has(file.ext)) total++;
  if (["a", "b"].includes(file.ext)) total++;
}
if (["js", "jsx", "ts", "tsx"].includes(mode)) total++;

Set in codeguard.toml:

[codeguard.rules.CG-PERF-105]

docs.title: CG-QUAL-001: Mutable default argument
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: quality · Languages: Python

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
A default value is created once, when the function is defined, and shared by every call. Mutating it in one call leaks state into the next.

Reported:

def add(item, bucket=[]):
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket


def merge(a, *, extra={}, seen=set()):
    return {**a, **extra}

Not reported:

def add(item, bucket=None, size=0, name="x", flags=()):
    bucket = [] if bucket is None else bucket
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Default to None and create the value inside: def f(items=None): items = [] if items is None else items

docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-QUAL-001] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-QUAL-002: Exception silently swallowed
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: quality · Languages: Python

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
A bare except: or except Exception: whose body is only pass hides every error, including bugs, and makes failures impossible to diagnose. A bare except: also catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit.

Reported:

def load(path):
    try:
        return open(path).read()
    except:
        pass
    try:
        return int(path)
    except Exception:
        ...

Not reported:

import logging


def load(path):
    try:
        return open(path).read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    except Exception:
        logging.exception("could not read %s", path)
        raise

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Catch the specific exception you expect, and log or re-raise anything else: except ValueError: logger.warning(...).

docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-QUAL-002] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: quality · Languages: Python

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
High cyclomatic complexity means many paths through the code: harder to test, review, and change safely.

Reported:

def classify(x):
    if x == 0:
        return 0
    if x == 1:
        return 1
    if x == 2:
        return 2
    if x == 3:
        return 3
    if x == 4:
        return 4
    if x == 5:
        return 5
    if x == 6:
        return 6
    if x == 7:
        return 7
    if x == 8:
        return 8
    if x == 9:
        return 9
    if x == 10:
        return 10
    if x == 11:
        return 11
    if x == 12:
        return 12
    if x == 13:
        return 13
    if x == 14:
        return 14
    if x == 15:
        return 15
    return -1

Not reported:

def classify(x):
    if x == 1:
        return 1
    return {2: 2, 3: 3}.get(x, -1)

docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: quality · Languages: Python

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Deeply nested blocks are hard to follow and usually hide a missing abstraction.

Reported:

def walk(tree):
    for a in tree:
        if a:
            for b in a:
                if b:
                    while b:
                        if b > 1:
                            b -= 1

Not reported:

def walk(tree):
    for a in tree:
        if not a:
            continue
        for b in a:

docs.title: CG-QUAL-005: Function takes too many parameters
docs.text: Severity: INFO · Category: quality · Languages: Python

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Long parameter lists are easy to call wrongly and suggest the function does too much.

Reported:

def connect(host, port, user, password, database, timeout, retries, ssl, *, verbose=False):
    pass

Not reported:

class Client:
    def connect(self, host, port, user, password, database, timeout, retries, ssl):
        pass

docs.title: CG-QUAL-101: Loose equality (== / !=)
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: quality · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript · Autofix: safe (how it works)

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
== and != convert types before comparing ('' == 0 and '0' == false are both true). Strict === and !== compare without conversion.

Reported:

if (typeof value == "string") run();
if (items.length != 0) run();
if (status == 200) run();

Not reported:

if (value == null) run();
if (value != undefined) run();
if (status === 200) run();

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Use === (convert explicitly first if needed).

codeguard scan --fix (or the editor quick fix) rewrites the example to:

if (typeof value === "string") run();
if (items.length !== 0) run();
if (status == 200) run();

docs.title: CG-QUAL-102: Empty catch block
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: quality · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
An empty catch block discards the error. Failures become silent and very hard to diagnose.

Reported:

try {
  risky();
} catch (err) {}

Not reported:

try {
  risky();
} catch (err) {
  // optional feature: absence is fine
}
try {
  risky();
} catch (err) {
  console.error(err);
}

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Handle the error, log it, or leave a comment explaining why it is safe to ignore.

docs.title: CG-QUAL-103: Function is too complex
docs.text: Severity: LOW · Category: quality · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
High cyclomatic complexity means many paths through the code: harder to test, review, and change safely.

Reported:

function classify(x) {
  if (x === 0) return 0;
  if (x === 1) return 1;
  if (x === 2) return 2;
  if (x === 3) return 3;
  if (x === 4) return 4;
  if (x === 5) return 5;
  if (x === 6) return 6;
  if (x === 7) return 7;
  if (x === 8) return 8;
  if (x === 9) return 9;
  if (x === 10) return 10;
  if (x === 11) return 11;
  if (x === 12) return 12;
  if (x === 13) return 13;
  if (x === 14) return 14;
  if (x === 15) return 15;
  return -1;
}

Not reported:

function classify(x) {
  return { 1: 1, 2: 2 }[x] ?? -1;
}

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Extract branches into well-named helper functions, or use a lookup object instead of long if/else chains.

docs.text:
Set in codeguard.toml:

[codeguard.rules.CG-QUAL-103]

docs.title: CG-QUAL-104: var declaration
docs.text: Severity: INFO · Category: quality · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
var is function-scoped and hoisted, so a variable is visible (as undefined) before its declaration and leaks out of blocks and loops.

Reported:

var count = 0;
for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) count++;

Not reported:

let count = 0;
const limit = 3;
for (let i = 0; i < limit; i++) count++;

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Use const, or let if the variable is reassigned.
