docs.title: CG-SEC-001: SQL Injection via String Formatting
Description
docs.text: Detects SQL queries constructed using f-strings, .format(), or % string formatting with user-controlled input. This allows attackers to manipulate the query logic, bypass authentication, or exfiltrate data.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-89 — Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
  • OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
def get_user(uid):
    query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {uid}"
    cursor.execute(query)

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
def get_user(uid):
    cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (uid,))

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Always use parameterized queries or prepared statements. Never concatenate or interpolate user input directly into SQL strings.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Detects hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens, and secrets assigned directly to variables. Hardcoded credentials embedded in source code can be exposed via version control history or code leaks.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-798 — Use of Hard-coded Credentials
  • OWASP: A07:2021 — Identification and Authentication Failures

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
api_key = "sk-abc123xyz"
password = "supersecret123"

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
import os
api_key = os.environ.get("API_KEY")
password = os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD")

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Load secrets from environment variables, a secrets manager (e.g. AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault), or a .env file that is excluded from version control.

docs.title: CG-SEC-003: Use of eval() or exec()
Description
docs.text: Detects calls to eval() or exec() with dynamic or user-controlled input. These functions execute arbitrary Python code and can be exploited to run malicious commands on the server.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-95 — Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code
  • OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
user_input = input("Enter expression: ")
result = eval(user_input)

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
import ast
result = ast.literal_eval(user_input)  # Only safe for literals

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Avoid eval() and exec() entirely. Use ast.literal_eval() for safe literal parsing, or redesign the logic to avoid dynamic code execution.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Detects use of pickle.loads() on untrusted data or yaml.load() without SafeLoader. Deserializing untrusted data with these functions can lead to arbitrary code execution.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-502 — Deserialization of Untrusted Data
  • OWASP: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
import pickle
obj = pickle.loads(data_from_network)

import yaml
config = yaml.load(file_content)

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
import yaml
config = yaml.safe_load(file_content)

import json
data = json.loads(file_content)  # prefer JSON over pickle

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Never unpickle data from untrusted sources. Use yaml.safe_load() instead of yaml.load(). Prefer JSON or other safe formats for data exchange.

docs.title: CG-SEC-005: subprocess with shell=True and Variable Input
Description
docs.text: Detects calls to subprocess.run(), subprocess.call(), or subprocess.Popen() with shell=True and a dynamic (non-literal) command string. This can allow command injection if user input reaches the command.

docs.title: Security Risk
docs.text:
• CWE: CWE-78 — Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
  • OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: Vulnerable Example
docs.text:
import subprocess
filename = input("Enter filename: ")
subprocess.run(f"cat {filename}", shell=True)

docs.title: Safe Example
docs.text:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(["cat", filename])  # list form, no shell

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Pass commands as a list instead of a string to avoid shell interpretation. If shell=True is required, ensure the command string is fully static and never includes user-controlled input.

docs.title: CG-SEC-006: Weak hash (MD5 / SHA-1) used for a security value
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: security · Languages: Python CWE: CWE-328 · OWASP: A02:2021 — Cryptographic Failures

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security purposes: collisions are practical and both are fast enough to brute-force passwords. The surrounding names suggest this hash protects a password, token, or signature.

Reported:

# MD5 / SHA-1 protecting passwords and tokens.
import hashlib
from hashlib import sha1


def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest()


def make_reset_token(user_id: int) -> str:
    return sha1(str(user_id).encode()).hexdigest()


api_signature = hashlib.new("MD5", b"payload").hexdigest()

Not reported:

# Checksums, cache keys, opted-out calls, and strong hashes do not trigger.
import hashlib


def cache_key(url: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.md5(url.encode()).hexdigest()


def file_checksum(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()


def legacy_password_lookup(password: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.md5(password.encode(), usedforsecurity=False).hexdigest()


def hash_token(token: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Hash passwords with a slow, salted KDF (hashlib.scrypt, argon2, bcrypt). For tokens and signatures use hashlib.sha256 or hmac with SHA-256. If this is not security-related, pass usedforsecurity=False.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-006] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-SEC-007: TLS certificate verification disabled
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: Python CWE: CWE-295 · OWASP: A07:2021 — Identification and Authentication Failures

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Certificate verification is turned off, so the connection accepts any certificate. Anyone on the network path can read and modify the traffic.

Reported:

# TLS certificate verification turned off.
import ssl

import httpx
import requests

requests.get("https://internal.example", verify=False)
client = httpx.Client(verify=False)
ctx = ssl._create_unverified_context()

context = ssl.create_default_context()
context.check_hostname = False
context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE


def fetch(session):
    return session.post("https://api.example", json={}, verify=False)

Not reported:

# Verification on, or a custom CA bundle.
import ssl

import requests

requests.get("https://internal.example", verify="/etc/ssl/internal-ca.pem")
requests.get("https://example.com")
context = ssl.create_default_context(cafile="ca.pem")
context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_REQUIRED
options = {"verify": False}  # a plain dict, not a request

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Keep certificate verification on. To trust a private CA, pass its bundle: requests.get(url, verify='/path/to/ca.pem') or ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...).

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-007] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-SEC-008: Insecure temporary file name (tempfile.mktemp)
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: security · Languages: Python CWE: CWE-377 · OWASP: A01:2021 — Broken Access Control

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
tempfile.mktemp() returns a file name without creating the file. Between the call and the open, another process can create or symlink that path (a race).

Reported:

import tempfile
from tempfile import mktemp

path = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".txt")
other = mktemp()

Not reported:

import tempfile

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".txt")
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) as fh:
    name = fh.name

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Create the file atomically: tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False), tempfile.mkstemp(), or tempfile.mkdtemp() for a private directory.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-008] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-SEC-009: random module used for a security value
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: security · Languages: Python · Autofix: safe (how it works) CWE: CWE-338 · OWASP: A02:2021 — Cryptographic Failures

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
The random module is not cryptographically secure: an attacker who sees some outputs can predict the rest. The surrounding names suggest this value is a token, password, or secret.

Reported:

"""Tokens and passwords from the random module."""

import random
import string

ALPHABET = string.ascii_letters + string.digits


def make_password(length: int = 16) -> str:
    return "".join(random.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(length))


session_token = random.getrandbits(128)
otp = random.randint(100000, 999999)

Not reported:

# Non-security randomness (simulation, shuffling, jitter) does not trigger.
import random
import secrets

dice = random.randint(1, 6)
jitter = random.uniform(0, 0.5)
deck = list(range(52))
random.shuffle(deck)
token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Use the secrets module: secrets.token_urlsafe(32) for tokens, secrets.choice(seq) to pick, secrets.randbelow(n) for integers.

codeguard scan --fix (or the editor quick fix) rewrites the example to:

"""Tokens and passwords from the random module."""

import random
import string
import secrets

ALPHABET = string.ascii_letters + string.digits


def make_password(length: int = 16) -> str:
    return "".join(secrets.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(length))


session_token = secrets.randbits(128)
otp = random.randint(100000, 999999)

The autofix is applied only when it is provably equivalent: random.choice -> secrets.choice, random.getrandbits -> secrets.randbits, random.randbytes -> secrets.token_bytes (identical signatures), adding import secrets when needed. Other functions get a suggestion only.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: # codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-009] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-SEC-010: Untrusted input reaches a SQL query
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: Python · Analysis: taint tracking CWE: CWE-89 · OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Request data or process input that flows, through any number of assignments and string operations, into cursor.execute() / executemany() / executescript().

from flask import request

def search(db):
    term = request.args.get("q")                    # source
    sql = "SELECT * FROM items WHERE name = '" + term + "'"
    db.execute(sql)                                 # sink -> CG-SEC-010

The finding lists the source and every assignment on the way, in the terminal, SARIF (relatedLocations), and editor diagnostics. On the same line it replaces the pattern rule CG-SEC-001, so you get one finding with the full path.

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Pass values as query parameters.

db.execute("SELECT * FROM items WHERE name = ?", (term,))

Wrapping the value in int() / float() is recognised as sanitizing.

docs.title: CG-SEC-011: Untrusted input reaches a shell command
docs.text: Severity: CRITICAL · Category: security · Languages: Python · Analysis: taint tracking CWE: CWE-78 · OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Untrusted data in a command run through the shell: os.system, os.popen, subprocess.getoutput / getstatusoutput, and subprocess.* with shell=True. Replaces CG-SEC-005 on the same line.

host = request.form["host"]
os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)   # host = "8.8.8.8; rm -rf ~"

Request data gives confidence 0.85. Process input (sys.argv, environment, input()) gives 0.6, since only the invoking user controls it.

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", host])        # no shell
os.system("ping -c 1 " + shlex.quote(host))      # if a shell is unavoidable

docs.title: CG-SEC-012: Untrusted input reaches eval() / exec()
docs.text: Severity: CRITICAL · Category: security · Languages: Python · Analysis: taint tracking CWE: CWE-95 · OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Untrusted data passed to eval(), exec(), or compile(). Replaces CG-SEC-003 on the same line.

expr = request.json["expr"]
result = eval(expr)

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Never execute input as code. Parse data with json.loads() or ast.literal_eval(), and dispatch with a dict of allowed functions.

docs.title: CG-SEC-013: Request data used as a file path
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: Python · Analysis: taint tracking CWE: CWE-22 · OWASP: A01:2021 — Broken Access Control

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Request data used as the path of open(), os.open/remove/unlink/rename/listdir, shutil.*, pathlib.Path(), or flask.send_file(). A name like ../../etc/passwd escapes the intended directory.

name = request.args["file"]
return send_file(os.path.join("/srv/files", name))

Only request data counts. A command-line tool opening the file its user named is expected behaviour and is not reported. flask.send_from_directory() is not a sink, because it joins paths safely.

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename
name = secure_filename(request.args["file"])         # or os.path.basename()

path = (BASE / name).resolve()
if not path.is_relative_to(BASE):
    abort(404)

docs.title: CG-SEC-014: Request data used as a redirect target
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: security · Languages: Python · Analysis: taint tracking CWE: CWE-601 · OWASP: A01:2021 — Broken Access Control

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
A redirect whose URL comes from the request: flask.redirect(), Django redirect() / HttpResponseRedirect(), and Starlette / FastAPI RedirectResponse().

return redirect(request.args.get("next"))   # ?next=https://evil.example

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Redirect only to relative paths or an allow-list of hosts. Django provides url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(). Allow-list checks are not visible to the analysis; suppress with a reason once the check is in place.

docs.title: CG-SEC-101: Dynamic code execution
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-95 · OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
eval(x), new Function(..., body), and setTimeout("...") / setInterval("...") where the code string is not a literal. Passing a string to a timer is an implicit eval.

eval(userInput);
const fn = new Function("a", body);
setTimeout("refresh(" + id + ")", 1000);

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Do not execute strings as code. Use a lookup table of functions, dynamic import(), or pass a function (not a string) to setTimeout / setInterval.

const handlers = { refresh, reload };
handlers[name]?.();
setTimeout(() => refresh(id), 1000);

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: eval(trusted); // codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-101] reason: build-time constant

docs.title: CG-SEC-102: child_process.exec with a dynamic command
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-78 · OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
child_process.exec / execSync run their argument through /bin/sh. A non-literal command lets an attacker inject shell syntax.

const { exec } = require("child_process");
exec(`git checkout ${branch}`);

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Use execFile() / spawn() with an argument array and no shell.

execFile("git", ["checkout", branch]);

docs.title: CG-SEC-103: DOM XSS sink assigned a non-literal
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-79 · OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
el.innerHTML = x, el.outerHTML = x, el.insertAdjacentHTML(pos, x), and document.write(x) / writeln(x) where the HTML is not a string literal.

results.innerHTML = "<b>" + query + "</b>";

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Set textContent, build nodes with DOM APIs, or sanitize with DOMPurify first.

results.textContent = query;
results.innerHTML = DOMPurify.sanitize(html); // codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-103] reason: sanitized

docs.title: CG-SEC-104: dangerouslySetInnerHTML with a non-literal value
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript (JSX/TSX) CWE: CWE-79 · OWASP: A03:2021 — Injection

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text: <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: value }} /> with a non-literal value, which bypasses React's XSS escaping.

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Render the value as text, or sanitize it with DOMPurify before passing it to __html.

<div>{comment.body}</div>

docs.title: CG-SEC-105: Hardcoded secret
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-798 · OWASP: A07:2021 — Identification and Authentication Failures

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
A non-trivial string literal assigned to an identifier, property, or object key whose name reads like a credential (password, apiKey, token, clientSecret, …). Mirrors the Python rule CG-SEC-002. Confidence is 0.9 because placeholder values in examples can trip it.

const apiKey = "sk_live_51H8...";

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Load secrets from process.env or a secrets manager; never commit them.

const apiKey = process.env.STRIPE_API_KEY;

docs.title: CG-SEC-106: Math.random() used for a security value
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-338

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Math.random() used to build a token, session id, password, nonce, salt, OTP, or API key. The rule fires only when the surrounding binding name signals a security use (confidence 0.8).

const resetToken = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text:
Use a cryptographically secure source.

const resetToken = crypto.randomUUID();
const bytes = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));

docs.title: CG-SEC-107: Weak hash (MD5 / SHA-1) used for a security value
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-328 · OWASP: A02:2021 — Cryptographic Failures

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security: collisions are practical and both are fast enough to brute-force passwords. The surrounding names suggest this hash protects a password, token, or signature.

Reported:

const crypto = require("crypto");

function hashPassword(password) {
  return crypto.createHash("md5").update(password).digest("hex");
}

const apiSignature = crypto.createHash("sha1").update(body).digest("hex");

Not reported:

const crypto = require("crypto");

const etag = crypto.createHash("md5").update(body).digest("hex");
function hashPassword(password, salt) {
  return crypto.scryptSync(password, salt, 64).toString("hex");
}
const token = crypto.createHash("sha256").update(seed).digest("hex");

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Hash passwords with a slow KDF (crypto.scrypt, argon2, bcrypt). For tokens and signatures use crypto.createHmac('sha256', key) or createHash('sha256').

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: // codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-107] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-SEC-108: TLS certificate verification disabled
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-295 · OWASP: A07:2021 — Identification and Authentication Failures

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Certificate verification is turned off, so the connection accepts any certificate. Anyone on the network path can read and modify the traffic.

Reported:

const https = require("https");

const agent = new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: false });
request({ url, strictSSL: false });
process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = "0";

Not reported:

const https = require("https");
const fs = require("fs");

const agent = new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: fs.readFileSync("ca.pem") });
process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = "1";

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Keep verification on. To trust a private CA, pass it explicitly: new https.Agent({ ca: fs.readFileSync('ca.pem') }) or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: // codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-108] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-SEC-109: Redirect to a URL taken from the request
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-601 · OWASP: A01:2021 — Broken Access Control

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
The redirect target comes from the request or the page URL. Attackers use this to send victims from a trusted domain to a phishing site (open redirect).

Reported:

app.get("/login/done", (req, res) => {
  res.redirect(req.query.next);
});

app.post("/go", (req, res) => res.redirect(302, req.body.url));

const target = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("return");
location.href = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("return");

Not reported:

app.get("/login/done", (req, res) => {
  res.redirect("/home");
});
location.href = "/dashboard";

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Redirect only to relative paths or an allow-list of origins, e.g. const u = new URL(next, base); if (u.origin === base) res.redirect(u.pathname).

docs.title: Suppress
docs.text: // codeguard: ignore[CG-SEC-109] reason: <why this is fine>

docs.title: CG-SEC-110: File path built from request data
docs.text: Severity: HIGH · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-22 · OWASP: A01:2021 — Broken Access Control

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
A file path is built from request data. Sequences like '../' let an attacker read or overwrite files outside the intended directory (path traversal).

Reported:

import fs from "fs";
import path from "path";

app.get("/file", (req, res) => {
  const data = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, "files", req.query.name as string));
  res.send(data);
});

app.get("/download/:name", (req, res) => {
  res.download(`/srv/files/${req.params.name}`);
});

app.delete("/upload", async (req, res) => {
  await fs.promises.unlink("/tmp/" + req.body.file);
});

Not reported:

import fs from "fs";
import path from "path";

app.get("/file", (req, res) => {
  const data = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, "files", path.basename(req.query.name as string)));
  res.sendFile(req.params.name, { root: "/srv/files" });
  fs.readFileSync("/etc/app/config.json");
});

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Reduce the value to a file name with path.basename(), then resolve it and check it stays inside the base directory: if (!full.startsWith(base + path.sep)) reject.

docs.title: CG-SEC-111: Deep merge of request data (prototype pollution)
docs.text: Severity: MEDIUM · Category: security · Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript CWE: CWE-1321 · OWASP: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures

docs.title: What it catches
docs.text:
Request data is deep-merged into an object. A key such as 'proto' can modify Object.prototype and change behaviour across the whole application.

Reported:

const _ = require("lodash");

app.post("/settings", (req, res) => {
  _.merge(userSettings, req.body);
  $.extend(true, defaults, req.body.prefs);
});

Not reported:

const _ = require("lodash");

app.post("/settings", (req, res) => {
  Object.assign(userSettings, { theme: req.body.theme });
  _.merge(userSettings, defaults);
  $.extend(defaults, req.body);
});

docs.title: How to fix
docs.text: Copy only the fields you expect (const { name, email } = req.body), validate the body with a schema, or merge into Object.create(null). Keep lodash >= 4.17.21.
